posts.content:
Figma’s Q2’26 was another record quarter.

We’re building the canvas for full stack creation, and it’s resonating with our customers.

Revenue was $370M, up 48% YoY and our third straight quarter of accelerated YoY revenue growth.

We’re raising our full-year revenue guidance by $40M to between $1.463B and $1.467B, implying 39% YoY growth at the midpoint. The raise is reflective of strength in 1) AI credit consumption 2) positive early signal on the back of our new launches 3) strong conversion and 4) continued expansion.

We’re confident how this will compound in the quarters ahead. AI is changing how teams build software and how creative work is done, and that makes Figma even more important.

Strong finish, and a big year ahead!

Incredible day of launches at #Config 2026. New creative materials, agentic tools, and a canvas that just got a lot more powerful.

As code gets easier to write, value moves up the stack — to the layer where decisions get made and design happens. That's what Figma is built for. The infinite canvas is where the world's best teams explore, riff, iterate, and ship products that stand out. Today, we made it even more powerful.

We're bringing new materials like code, shaders, and motion directly to the canvas, giving teams more expression in the products they build. With Weave, AI becomes a creative material in its own right: something you shape, push, and refine until it looks and feels exactly right.

But materials are only half the story. The other half is moving faster with intelligent tools. Agent skills and generative plugins make the canvas smarter. It learns your process, adapts to how you work, whether you're running a specific task or inventing a tool from scratch.

All of this creates tremendous value for our customers and unlocks exciting new opportunities for Figma. So proud of the team for their hustle and execution.

posts.content:
It’s not often you’re given the opportunity to reshape the lives of millions. I’ve had the privilege of contributing to the mission and vision we’ve had here at Figma and playing a role in building something I couldn’t be more proud to stand behind. 

Today, we share our intention to accelerate on our journey jointly with the team at Adobe. Adobe software has been the standard for creatives all over the world for 40 years. Bringing our teams together represents an opportunity to accelerate the growth and innovation of the Figma platform with access to Adobe’s technology, expertise and resources for the betterment of both sets of customers and an industry at large. 

What’s been exciting to me through the conversations with Adobe leaders — Shantanu, David, Dan, Scott and Gloria — is this idea that this deal is different. Shantanu and David have spoken to a joint vision that celebrates the “superpowers” of each organization and empowering the leaders here at Figma to continue to execute against our vision with a similar spirit and clear authority. 

To the Figma team, community, supporters and partners, let’s celebrate this moment together. Our every intention is to continue to deliver and delight. The long term vision has never wavered. Continue to expect the best out of this team, as I certainly will.

Our strong numbers got a lot of the attention in yesterday’s earnings report, so you might have missed that architects are now designing renderings in Figma Weave and that we closed one of the largest deals in Figma's 14-year history.

At NBBJ, one of the world’s leading architecture firms, architects are using Figma Weave to generate and refine photorealistic renderings. What used to take days and an external studio now happens in-house, in real time. Adoption of Weave at NBBJ is expected to triple over the next three months.

In Q1, we also saw one of the world’s largest hyperscalers consolidate thousands of product and engineering teams across dozens of business units into a single Figma agreement with more than 35,000 paid seats. This was one of the largest deals for Figma ever. 

The pattern is clear: We’re seeing customers go bigger and broader in Figma as value moves up the stack to design.
